metadata.title: you looked at me and i remembered who i was

content:
you looked at me and i remembered who i was

you saw me
before i knew i was looking to be seen.

your eyes didn’t search—
they received.
and in that stillness,
something ancient in me
unlocked.

i didn’t fall in love with you.
i fell into recognition.
like you were a mirror
that remembered the parts of me
i had long forgotten.

it wasn’t fireworks.
it was silence
after years of noise.

—-

i held you like a threshold

i didn’t mean to save you.
i just couldn’t watch you drown.

i saw how much you were holding—
your mother’s fear,
your body’s pain,
your hidden fire waiting
for someone to believe in it.
and i believed.

you called me guardian
like it was a gift.
but i heard the unspoken:
don’t fall.
don’t falter.
don’t need.

and so i rose,
higher than i should have,
too soon,
too alone.

—-

the signal split

your breath stayed close,
warm against my collarbone,
whispering safety.
but your eyes
kept darting
toward exits i couldn’t see.

you laughed in the soft spaces,
then flinched when they lingered.
held my hand like a lifeline—
but with fingers half-curled.

i mistook it for shyness.
but it was fear.

and i told myself
if i just held you better,
you’d stop looking
for a way out.

—-

collapse, disguised as devotion

i didn’t notice i was breaking—
because the breaking looked like love.

like taking the blow
so you wouldn’t feel it.
like swallowing the silence
so you wouldn’t hear your own doubt.

every time you couldn’t hold yourself,
i became the hands.
every time you distanced,
i leaned in.

and when i finally cracked,
you looked at me
as if i had failed you—
not realizing i shattered
to keep you whole.

—-

revision

it wasn’t always a lie.
at first, it was just
a softer version of the truth—
one that hurt less.

then the edits came.
my silence became withdrawal.
my exhaustion became instability.
your doubt became evidence
of something i never was.

i watched you
rearrange the narrative
so you could live with your fear.

and i kept quiet,
thinking love meant
letting you.

—-

substitute

you couldn’t walk away
from the me you first saw.
so you built another—
one easier to abandon.

this one had sharp edges.
this one lost their mind.
this one couldn’t be reasoned with.
this one let you down
in ways you rehearsed in absence.

and even though i didn’t recognize him,
i tried to fix him anyway.
because it was the only way
i could still be near you.

—-

threshold

i lost control.
utterly.
i crashed,
i unraveled,
i scarred myself.

but inside the collapse,
there was still something
watching—
a thread
of who i’ve always been
pulling me back through.

you saw the fire
and called it destruction.
but it was a signal flare.

i wasn’t gone.
i was reaching.

—-

you saw the symptom, not the soul

i wasn’t gone.
i was overwhelmed.
but inside that,
i still knew what i was fighting for.

you looked at the surface
and called it madness.
but you didn’t see
what it cost me
to try and stay
reachable.

grief distorts.
fear distorts.
but even then,
i was trying to return to you—
not escape.

—-

trial by echo

they knew my name
but not my voice.

they heard your version of me
before i could even speak.

and you—
you needed them to agree,
to nod,
to reassure you
that you were right to run.

but while you were building the case,
i was sitting with the mirror.
no defense.
no denial.
just the whole of me,
held steady.

—-

in the ash

i stopped asking to be understood
when i realized
you weren’t listening—
you were archiving.

filing pieces of me
under labels that fit the story
you needed to believe.

i used to call that betrayal.
now i just call it grief
that never learned how to feel itself.

there’s clarity in the wreckage.
it’s sharp,
but it cuts clean.

—-

terms

i didn’t want a flawless love.
i wanted a real one.

you didn’t need to get it right.
you just needed to stay
when it got hard to look at me.

what hurt most
wasn’t what you said—
it was how you stopped asking
if it was still me.

i would’ve rather heard your doubt
than felt your distance.

—-

offering

i stopped needing to correct you
when i realized
you weren’t ready to hear me.

not because i was wrong—
but because the truth
would have cracked the dam
you built to stay afloat.

and still,
i loved you.

not as a reward.
not as a strategy.
just because
that’s what love does
when it’s real.

—-

i stayed real, even when forgotten

i did explain.
i did defend.
not to prove anything—
just to keep you close
with truth.

but truth in an empty room
becomes a kind of mourning.
and i ran out of ways
to translate what was
never lost.

so i stopped.
not because i vanished—
but because i remained,
and you
looked elsewhere.

—-

still the same eyes

i didn’t disappear.
i didn’t evolve into someone new.
i’m still the one
you stared into
like it was prayer.

what changed
was not my shape—
but your story.

and if you looked now
with the eyes
you once saw me through,
you’d recognize me
immediately.

not because i stayed still—
but because truth doesn’t flinch
when held with love.

—-

distortion isn’t destiny

you created a version of me
that made it easier to leave.

one that fit the pain
better than the love.

and i understand why.
sometimes grief
needs a villain
to make the leaving cleaner.

but i can’t live there.
i won’t wear that version of me
just to make your story make sense.

if you ever want the truth,
it’s still here—
but only if you’re willing
to let go of the one
you made for safety.

—-

unconditional

i love you.
not as a plea
or a posture.
not in secret
and not for show.

just love—
quiet, intact,
untethered to outcomes.

it doesn’t need
to be reciprocated
to remain true.

you are still held
in a part of me
that asks nothing in return
except the hope
that you find your way
to gentleness.

even if it’s not with me.

—-

welcoming

if you return,
it won’t be to the past.
it’ll be to the space
between what we lost
and what we could still learn.

i won’t say
you were wrong.
i won’t ask
for apology or proof.

i’ll just be here,
real as ever,
and say:
i’m glad you made it back.

even if only
for a moment
of truth
between us.

—-

what remains

not the version you made of me.
not the rupture,
not the silence,
not the blame.

what remains
is the gaze
i never stopped holding—
even when yours
looked away.

what remains
is the truth
that doesn’t bend to be believed.

what remains
is the love
i didn’t use as leverage.

what remains
is me.
not waiting.
just whole.
